notes: Background: LexaMesh runs search for a consortium of EU law firms; index contains many OCR PDFs, multi-language corpora.
Current stack: Elastic-based index with in-house 768-dim embeddings + lightweight BM25 candidate scorer; custom re-ranker built on a fine-tuned cross-encoder.
Pain points: cannot meet p95 latency under heavy load; cost of running cross-encoder on 20k queries/day is rising; indexing/replication overhead is high.
Scale ask: target index size 80M docs, 400M vectors (sharded at ingestion); seasonal peak QPS ~8k, sustained 2k.
Performance SLOs: end-to-end p50 <40ms, p95 <180ms when reranker on for top-20 candidates.
Cost target: target amortized cost per reranked query < $0.08 (EUR equivalent); CFO wants scenarios for 50%, 75%, 100% traffic.
Migration objective: replace in-house reranker with Redwood-hosted reranker (quantized candidate generator + distilled cross-encoder) but preserve or improve NDCG@10 baseline.

Evals plan: Redwood SE to run parallel evals: baseline vs candidate embedding families (fast-sim, dense-quant) + reranker variants; metrics: MRR, NDCG@1/5/10, latency and cost per query; human A/B judgments for 2k queries across practice areas.
Quality guardrails: client rule - no >2% drop in NDCG@10 and manual review required if drift detected; automatic rollback to legacy system allowed during canary.
Canary strategy requested: traffic ramp 0.5% -> 2% -> 10% -> 50% with monitoring on NDCG, CTR proxies, latency and error rates; immediate 0% rollback if NDCG delta > 1.5% for 1-hour window.

Technical constraints: their index format uses Elastic token offsets; need candidate mapping shim or re-index into Redwood-compatible vector layout. They prefer option to keep BM25 layer as fallback to reduce risk.
Security/legal: require ISO27001 evidence, on-prem connector architecture diagram, and a 90-day log retention export to customer Splunk instance.
Open question: whether to run deduplication/segment-level caching in front of Redwood reranker to reduce compute and cost.
Stakeholder quote: 'If the reranker migration doesn't meet our stringent NDCG requirements we won't pass the procurement gate.'
Procurement notes: procurement will require 3 quotes and a 60-day security review; prefer annual commitment with quarterly SLAs.
Action items: SE to produce throughput/cost estimates for Dedicated with 8 GPU nodes; build eval harness and seed 2k labeled queries; legal to receive SOC2/ISO artefacts (drive link).
